paper_metadata.title: Microstructure control and compressive strength of 10 mol% Ti-bearing Nb3Al/Nbss in-situ composites

evidence.quote: 10 mol% Ti-bearing Nb 3Al()/Nbss() in-situ composites with ﬁne and homogeneous microstructures have been successfully fabricated by heat treatment or thermo-mechanical processing of cast ingots.

other.starting_materials: 99.86 mass% Nb, 99.99 mass% Al, 99.999 mass% Ti

evidence.quote: Button ingots with compositions Nb– xAl–10Ti (x = 5, 13, 17, 20) (compositions are given in mol% in this paper unless otherwise stated) were prepared by arc-melting under an Ar atmosphere, using 99.86 mass% niobium, 99.99 mass% aluminum and 99.999 mass% titanium as starting materials. The buttons were remelted more than twice to assure homogenization of constituent elements.

homogenization heat-treatment to eliminate solidiﬁcation structure was performed at 2173 K for 1 h in a vacuum of 2 10 ÿ3 Pa and followed by furnace cooling in a vacuum furnace equipped with a tungsten mesh heater (it took about 5 min in cooling from 2173 to 1273 K).
Alloys for compression tests were annealed at 1473 K for 170 h and in a vacuum of 1 10 ÿ3 Pa to obtain fully stable microstructure at maximum test temperature.
